decisionsTitle: «Vârstă» and «Oraș» on the «Voluntari» list; «Trimite și linkul pentru semnarea declarației» on the organizers' message; the organizers' words as a panel of their own, with bold; «Am notat că vii» apart from the cancel; «Vin» no longer called optional; three named emergency numbers on the bib, «112» included; and «Mărimea numelui» and «Banda dintr-un capăt în altul» on the bib (amending §338, §364, §695, §759, §839 and the decision «Cere reconfirmarea»)
decisionsSection:
Six lines of the owner's, 2026-11-16, one morning.

### Part one: «Vârstă» and «Oraș» on the «Voluntari» list

**The owner, 2026-11-16, over a picture of the «Voluntari» list:** «In lista de voluntari trebuie sa vad varsta si orasul».

**Decision.** The list (§839) gets two columns right after the name: «Vârstă» / "Age" and «Oraș» / "City". The age is the row's own `age` — the age on the event's day, the one the parent's agreement goes by (§773) — said as a bare number, as the registrations list says it (§660), with one line behind the heading's «?» saying which age it is; the city is the one the person typed. A person who gave neither (a name the club typed, a row from before §765) reads «—». Both headings sort, as the registrations list's do: the youngest first, the cities A to Z without regard to case — «brașov» stands beside «Brașov» —, and whoever gave no answer last, whichever way the column reads. Both are columns like any other: «Coloane» hides them (§661), and the phone cards carry a line for each.

**No new disclosure.** The list is read by the roles `canManageVolunteers` names, the same ones that already read both answers on the person's page and in the event's files; nothing public changes, and the two words in an address (`sort=age`, `sort=city`) are column names, never anybody's data.

**Refused.** One line under the name («34 de ani · Săcele») instead of two columns: it costs no width, but it cannot be sorted or hidden, and the registrations list — the shape this screen was asked to follow — has both as columns. The date of birth in the cell: the person's page has it, and the number is what is read down a column. Dropping «Alergări» while one event is chosen, as the registrations list does (§943), to give the width back: not asked — so on a screen narrower than about 1300 px the table is now a little wider than its frame and scrolls sideways inside it, the row's verbs pinned (§943).

### Part two: «Trimite și linkul pentru semnarea declarației»

**The owner, 2026-11-16, the same morning, about to write to everybody registered for the race five days away:** «azi vreau sa si trimit mail catre toti aprticipantii si lispeste o optiune: vreau ca cei care nu au semnat declaratia sa o poata semna, momentan e doar o persoana in situatia asta».

**What was missing.** «Trimite un mesaj participanților» (§364) reaches the registered who owe the declaration — they are one of its four groups, «Declarație nesemnată» — but its email gave them nothing to sign with: the link is in the declaration request they got earlier, and the ready reminder text could only say «urmează pașii din emailul primit». §943 had already given the confirmed their number and QR under the organizers' words; nothing gave the unsigned their link.

**Decision.** A third tick on the composer, «Trimite și linkul pentru semnarea declarației» / "Also send the link to sign the declaration", off by default, built as §943's tick is.

- **The send** puts a flag — never a link — on the outbox rows of the registrations that owe their declaration as it queues them (`PENDING_DECLARATION`: the composer's own group), a test row too, and counts them in its audit row (`signLink`, `withSignLink`, `withSignLinkTest`). Every other row is the words alone, and the club's one copy carries no flag (§320).
- **The renderer** asks again when each email leaves — a send drains over hours — and mints the link only for a row that carries the flag, at the registration's own address, for a registration that owes the declaration then, where «Nu mai pot ajunge» goes too: the event ahead and running (`organizerSignLinkApplies`, on top of `cannotComeApplies`). It is the declaration request's own link: purpose `COMPLETE_DECLARATION`, single use, hashed at rest, minted at send time, alive until the start (§160). It replaces the registration's earlier declaration link, as every newer link does (BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 5), and any offer link left from before the hold (§643): the tick's help line says so, since the button in the person's earlier email stops working.
- **The email** draws «Semnează declarația» / "Sign the declaration", filled, the card's width, with one sentence under it — above «Vin» and «Nu mai pot ajunge». The page it opens is the declaration's own, which asks whatever the request's page asks: nothing here signs, confirms or moves anything.
- **The screens.** The preview draws the button on an inert example link while the box is ticked (the example runner is confirmed and would not get it: the preview shows what it looks like, the help line says who gets it); «Mesaje trimise» says the send was ticked and for how many; a send to the people ticked hands the tick back with the words (§945); the guide's task has a step for it.

**Nothing of a rule moves.** No state, place, hold, deadline, the allocator or the capacity formula reads the flag — a test holds the list of files that name it, as §943's does. Nobody signs for anybody: the link opens the person's own declaration, as the request's link always did, and an approved declaration is still what the page shows.

**Refused.** The link for an open waiting-list offer too: its own email carries its link and its deadline, and a second link from a message to everybody would say nothing of that deadline. The link for everybody in the send, signed or not: a confirmed runner has nothing to sign. The manage page as the place to sign: it has no declaration on it, and building one there is a second way to sign. A new token purpose: the request's own already means exactly this.

### Part three: the organizers' words stand apart in the email, and bold is read in them

**The owner, the same hour, of the message's words in the email:** «si as vrea sa aiba alt font si alt backround acest mesaj, sa fie mai vizibil si sa pot edita cu rich text editor» — with, in the composer's box, `**„Vin”**` typed for bold.

**What was wrong.** The organizers' words were drawn as the platform's own paragraphs, in the same face and on the same ground, after one framing sentence: nothing told the eye what the organizers had written from what every message says. And §364 had decided «the text is plain … no `**` is read inside it», so the asterisks typed in the box would have gone out as asterisks to everybody.

**Decision.**

- **One panel for the whole message** (`data-email-part="organizer-words"`): a tinted ground, an edge on its left and a serif face a size above the body's (`brand.ts#EMAIL_ORGANIZER_WORDS`). No new colour: the ground and the edge are the secondary look's own shades, so another club's emails wear its own, and they are told apart from the blue band of a message's one fact (§580). The face is one every mail client has — a webfont is what a mail client drops. The pairs are held as sent and as Gmail's app inverts them. The club's copy keeps the panel: they are the organizers' words there too.
- **`**like this**` is bold in the organizers' words** — amending §364's item 3. Applied after escaping, as for the platform's own sentences (§189), so the marker can only wrap text already made safe; it hugs its words, so «2 ** 3» and a pair left open stay what was typed; the plain-text half drops the markers. `__` stays what was typed: underline is the platform's own marker (§309). One line under the body says how.

**Not in this change: the rich-text editor.** The owner asked for it in the same sentence, and for «Tradu din română» to keep working in it. It replaces the two boxes of the very screen a message to 181 people was about to be sent from, and with them the checks on the words, the payload, the preview, the ready reminder, the words kept after a trial and the translation's fields: its own change, after the send, not an hour before it. Bold by marker is what that morning could safely have.

### Part four: «Am notat că vii» stands apart from «Anulează înscrierea»

**The owner, minutes after the trial's first «Vin», with a picture of the page on a phone:** «Aici trebuie ceva spatiu, ca sa nu se confuzeze cumva ca anuleaza». On the registration's own page, the answer — «Am notat că vii — ne-ai răspuns…» — stood 68 pixels above «Poți anula această înscriere. Locul va fi eliberat imediat.» and its red button: on one phone screen, somebody who had just said they were coming read a cancellation under their answer.

**Decision.** The «Vii la …?» block keeps twice the room under it: 48 pixels to the rule and 48 from the rule to the cancel (32 in a family's card, which has no rule). Nothing else moves — the same words, the same cancel that asks first (§384), the same anchors the emails land on. The browser journey of «Vin» measures the gap.

**Refused.** Hiding the cancel after an answer: §558 wants it one tap from every email, and somebody who said yes may still have to say no. Folding it away: the email's «Nu mai pot ajunge» lands on it.

### Part five: «Vin» is no longer called optional in what a participant reads

**The owner, the same hour, having read the trial's email:** «nu scrie nicaieri ca "nu e obligatoriu", vreau sa incurajez oamenii sa reconfirme».

**What it amends.** The decision «Cere reconfirmarea» read the owner's earlier «…dar e opțional» into three sentences a participant sees: under the email's «Vin» button («Ne spui că vii. Nu e obligatoriu.»), under «Da, vin la cursă» on the registration's page («Răspunsul e opțional: dacă nu apeși…, nu se schimbă nimic la înscrierea ta.») and in the ready reminder text («„Vin” e opțional…»). Each told the reader, right at the button, that pressing it was not needed.

**Decision.** The three sentences now say what the answer is for and nothing about whether it is owed: «Ne spui că vii: așa știm pe cine așteptăm la start.»; «Răspunsul tău ne ajută să știm pe cine așteptăm la start.» (the catalogue key is `reconfirm.why`, no longer `reconfirm.optional`); «Durează o secundă, iar răspunsul tău ne ajută să pregătim startul.» The staff's filter help says «Cine nu răspunde rămâne înscris» in place of «Răspunsul e opțional».

**What does not change — the rule.** Answering is still optional in fact: nothing in a state, a place, a deadline, the allocator or the capacity formula reads the answer, and nobody is cancelled for not answering (`reconfirmation-never-leaves.test.ts`). So the words encourage and stop there: no sentence says the answer is required, and none says or hints that silence costs the place — the tests of the ready text and of the page's sentences refuse «opțional», «obligatoriu», "optional", "mandatory" and "required" alike, beside the words for losing a place they already refused. The organizers' screens still say plainly that nobody is cancelled automatically.

**Refused.** «…și te asiguri că ai locul rezervat», the wording first asked for: the place is kept whether or not the button is pressed, so the sentence would promise something the press does not do and threaten something the silence does not cost.

### Part six: a third emergency number on the race number, and «112» is a number

**The owner, the same day, with a picture of two trail races' numbers:** «mai trebuie o modificare pt BIB, trebuie sa pun 2 numere de telefon dedesubt si incers: salvamont si organizator» — and the three the club will print: the organizers', the mountain rescue's and the emergency number itself.

**What was there.** «Telefon pentru urgențe» (§750, §759) already prints a line under the name, upside down by default («Tipărit invers», the trail practice), with a label and two numbers, each with its own name. Two things were missing: a third number, and «112» — the line took only what «Telefon public» takes, six digits at least, so the emergency number read as no number at all and printed nothing.

**Decision.** A third number with its own name (`emergencyPhone3`, `emergencyPhone3Label`), in the same JSON column, printed on the same line after the second. A number on the bib may now be as short as three digits (`BIB_EMERGENCY_MIN_DIGITS`); the club's public phone keeps its floor of six. No migration: the design is one JSON column (§249).

**And how the line reads — the owner, an hour later:** «de fapt vreau asa: ajutor start/finish: , ajutor traseu: , salvamont, cu label customizabil». The names were the club's to type already; what did not match was the line around them. So, amending §759's «Coordonator 07xx / Medic 07yy»: each number stands after its own name **and a colon**, and a **bar** parts the numbers — a name may hold a «/» itself — as the second number in the owner's picture prints its own: «Ajutor start/finish: 07xx | Ajutor traseu: 07yy | Salvamont: 07zz». And the sheet's own word before them («Urgențe» / "Emergency") prints only while some number stands without a name: numbers that each say whose they are need no word in front, and the club's own label, when it types one, still prints. A design with one unnamed number prints as it did, bar aside; the three fit the number's width at the line's own size.

**The numbers are typed in the designer, never written here.** The repository is public; the tests use made-up numbers.

**Refused, for now.** A block of several lines with a telephone glyph, as the larger of the two examples prints it: the line's own row has a fixed height on every number (§750), and a taller block takes room from the number itself — a change to the layout of every bib, five days before a print, that nobody has looked at on paper.

### Part seven: «Mărimea numelui» and «Banda dintr-un capăt în altul» on the race number

**The owner, the same day, two lines:** «vreau ca numele alergatorului sa fie un pic mai mare» and «si banda cu Brasov runners vreau sa fie dintr-un capat in altul, ca si fundal».

**Decision.** Two choices in the designer, each off until the club makes it, so every number designed before prints as it did — nothing about a bib already approved changes by a release. No migration: two more keys of the one JSON column (§249).

**«Mărimea numelui»** (`nameScale`, in «Numele»): «Normală» — the 24 points every number printed, in its 44-point strip — «Mai mare» (30 points in 52) or «Cea mai mare» (36 in 60). The strip grows by what its line grows, and the number's area gives up exactly that (`bib-geometry.ts#BIB_NAME_STRIPS`): the name never covers the number, the profile or the small print. A desk spare's empty line (§444) keeps its place on the paper, with more room above it to write in.

**A larger size never cuts a name the normal one printed whole.** A name is one line, cut with «…» past the card's width, and a line half as large again holds a third fewer letters — so the larger sizes alone would have cut names the normal size prints whole. `bibNameFit` sets a name that does not fit at the largest size, to half a point, at which it does, never under «Normală»; a name too long even there is cut as it always was. Measured with the bold type's own table (`bib-header.ts#bibTitleWidth`, never narrower than either renderer sets a line), once for the sheet and the picture.

**«Banda dintr-un capăt în altul»** (`bandBleed`, in «Antet»): the coloured band reaches the paper's left, right and top edges through the white margin; its foot, the lockup, the race and its date stay where they are, and so does everything under the band. This amends the white margin §338 gave the card on all four sides (`BIB_MARGIN`, whose own words were «the band does not bleed to the edge») and goes back, for the band alone, on what §695 refused for a whole card: «A home printer cannot print the margin, and a bleed on one half of an A4 sheet and not the other is two designs». That reason still stands, and is why the tick is off by default and says so beside it: an office printer cannot print a page's last millimetres, so on a sheet of two the upper number shows a white edge at its top that the lower one — whose top is the cut — does not. It is the club's choice for a sheet taken to a print shop. Only the coloured band reaches the edge: a header picture and a member's whole card keep their shapes.

**The pictures of numbers already drawn.** The emergency line's new form (part six) draws the same design differently, so `BIB_DRAWING_VERSION` is 6 and every stamped picture gets a new address; the two choices need no raise of their own — the stamps hash the whole design (§748).

**Not done.** The file is still exactly A4, with no bleed beyond the trim and no crop marks for one: a print shop that trims after printing asks for three millimetres more round the page, which is a different file and its own decision. And the name's size was looked at in the picture, not on paper.
changelogLine: - **Volunteers' age and city on the list, a link to sign the declaration in the organizers' message, and that message more visible** — on «Voluntari», each person's age on the event's day and their city stand in columns beside the name, both sortable. On «Trimite un mesaj participanților», the new tick «Trimite și linkul pentru semnarea declarației» gives everybody who has not signed the declaration yet a «Semnează declarația» button in their email, each with their own link; and what you write is now drawn in a panel of its own, with another ground and face, where `**words**` between two asterisks are bold. And on a registration's own page, «Am notat că vii» now stands well apart from «Anulează înscrierea», so an answer is not read as a cancellation. The «Vin» button's sentence, the page's and the ready reminder text no longer say that answering is optional: they say what the answer is for. On the race number, «Telefon pentru urgențe» takes a third number, a short one such as 112 now prints, and each number reads «Name: number», with a bar between them and no «Urgențe:» in front when every number has a name. And two new choices in the number's designer, both off until you make them: «Mărimea numelui» («Mai mare», «Cea mai mare» — a long name is set smaller rather than cut) and «Banda dintr-un capăt în altul», which takes the coloured band to the paper's edges, for a sheet printed at a print shop. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given `/admin/volunteers`, then each row names the person's age — the row's `age`, the age on the event's day — under «Vârstă» / "Age" and the city as typed under «Oraș» / "City", «—» for a person who gave none, in the table and in the phone cards; both headings sort (`sort=age`, `sort=city`), the city without regard to case, and a row with no answer comes last whichever way the column reads (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a send of the organizers' message with «Trimite și linkul pentru semnarea declarației» / "Also send the link to sign the declaration" ticked, then the flag `signLink` — never a link — is on the outbox rows of exactly the registrations in `PENDING_DECLARATION` when it queues them, a test row too, and on no other row nor on the club's copy; the send's audit row carries `signLink`, `withSignLink` and `withSignLinkTest`, and «Mesaje trimise» says the tick and the real count; a send without the tick writes none of it; and no registration's state, place, hold or deadline moves (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an organizers' message whose row carries `signLink`, when it is rendered for a registration that owes its declaration then, at its own address, before the start of an event that runs, then it carries «Semnează declarația» / "Sign the declaration" above «Vin» and «Nu mai pot ajunge», on a `COMPLETE_DECLARATION` token minted for that email — only its SHA-256 stored, unused, expiring at the event's start, scoped to that registration — which invalidates the registration's earlier declaration link and marks it superseded; for a registration confirmed, cancelled or lapsed since, waiting or holding an offer, after the start, or on a club copy, no button is drawn and no declaration token is minted; the preview draws the button on an example address and mints nothing (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends the criterion that the organizers' words carry no emphasis (`DECISIONS.md` §364). Given an organizers' message, then its words are drawn in each half as one block `data-email-part="organizer-words"` — the ground, edge, ink and face of `EMAIL_ORGANIZER_WORDS`, the paragraphs and line breaks as typed — after the platform's framing sentence and before the event's button, on the club's copy too; `**words**` are bold, applied after escaping and only where the marker hugs its words, the markers dropped from the plain-text half, and `__` printed as typed; the panel's ink and edge clear AA and 3:1 on its ground, as sent and inverted (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends the wording of «Vin» (the decision «Cere reconfirmarea»). Given an organizers' message that asks for reconfirmation, the registration's own page and the ready reminder text, then the sentence under «Vin» / "I'm coming", the sentence under «Da, vin la cursă» (`Registrations.reconfirm.why`) and the ready text say what the answer is for and never that it is optional, required or owed, in both languages, and no sentence says that silence costs the place; nothing reads the answer but the backoffice, as before (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the registration's own page after «Vin» was answered, then the answer «Am notat că vii…» and the cancel block under it stand at least 100 pixels apart on a phone and on a desktop, the cancel still on the page and asking first (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends the emergency line (`DECISIONS.md` §750, §759). Given «Telefon pentru urgențe» ticked, then the line prints up to three numbers in their order — the third `emergencyPhone3` with `emergencyPhone3Label` — each after its own name and a colon when it has one, a bar between them, on the sheet and in the picture alike, upside down while «Tipărit invers» is ticked; the club's label prints before them when typed, and with none the sheet's language's word prints only while some number has no name; a number is kept when it is written like a telephone number with three to fifteen digits, so «112» prints, and anything else reads as none; the club's public phone still needs six digits (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends the band inside the margin (`DECISIONS.md` §338, §695). Given a design with «Mărimea numelui» / "Name size" at `large` or `larger`, then the name prints at 30 or 36 points in a strip of 52 or 60, the number's area shorter by what the strip grew, on the sheet and in the picture alike; a name wider than the card at that size is set at the largest size, to half a point, at which it fits whole, never under the 24 points of `normal`, where a name too long is cut with «…» as before; and a desk spare's empty line keeps its place on the paper. Given «Banda dintr-un capăt în altul» / "The band from edge to edge" ticked, then the coloured band is drawn from the paper's left edge to its right and up to its top, its foot and the header's words unmoved, and never for a header picture or a member's card. A design saved before either key reads `normal` and unticked and draws as it did (2026-11-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the volunteers' age and city on the list; a link to sign the declaration in the organizers' message; that message as a panel of its own, with bold; «Am notat că vii» apart from the cancel; «Vin» no longer called optional; three named emergency numbers on the bib; «Mărimea numelui» and «Banda dintr-un capăt în altul» on the bib
